title: Template for the public summary of training content of GPAI models

covered_actors: providers of general-purpose AI models released under free and open-source licenses

evidence.quote: Article 53(1)(d) AI Act requires all providers of general-purpose AI models to draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed public summary of the content used for the training of the model
the objective of the Summary is to increase transparency on the content used for the training of general-purpose AI models, including text and data protected by law
The Template consists of three main sections: 1. General information... 2. List of data sources... 3. Relevant data processing aspects

Providers of general-purpose AI models shall […] draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training of the general-purpose AI model, according to a template provided by the AI Office
the AI Office to provide a template for the summary, which should be simple, effective, and allow the provider to provide the required summary in narrative form

compliance_deadlines: 2 August 2025 - rules under Section 2 of Chapter V AI Act apply, including Article 53(1)(d) obligation
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: This document is a template and explanatory notice issued by the AI Office under Article 53(1)(d) of the EU AI Act, requiring all GPAI model providers to publish a public summary of training content. The template has three sections: general information, list of data sources, and relevant data processing aspects. Providers may voluntarily disclose more than the minimum required. The open-source exception under Article 53(2) does not apply to this obligation. A voluntary 'upon request' mechanism for rightsholders regarding domain names not listed in the summary is recommended but not mandatory.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document frames training data transparency primarily as a mechanism to protect and enable the exercise of fundamental rights under EU law, including intellectual property rights, data subject rights, non-discrimination, cultural diversity, freedom of information, and freedom of science. Governance obligations are justified by enabling rightsholders and affected parties to exercise and enforce their legal rights.

evidence_spans.quote: transparency of the data used for the model training should help rightsholders obtain relevant information...needed to facilitate the exercise of their fundamental right to intellectual property and the fundamental right to an effective remedy

transparency of the general characteristics of the content used for training may also assist providers...to ensure that the fundamental rights to non-discrimination and language and cultural diversity are respected
greater transparency of the training data may also facilitate the fundamental right to receive and impart information and allow researchers to exercise their freedom of science
